key_insight: VISTA shows that multimodal models can do much better at interactive reasoning when they are given a visual harness that preserves what they have seen and lets them revisit it later. In short: the model's reasoning is strong; the right memory and perception setup unlocks it.
problem_solved: This paper addresses the challenge of making general-purpose multimodal models effective in long-horizon, interactive environments where important visual information can be missed, forgotten, or corrupted by text-only summaries.
method: Provides direct visual observation of the environment so the model can perceive state changes without relying only on text.
Maintains a lossless visual memory that stores past observations in their original form.
Supports active retrieval of prior visual information to help reasoning across long interactive sequences.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, VISTA suggests that better harness design can substantially improve multimodal agents without changing the base model itself. This is useful for building more reliable systems for robotics, games, GUI agents, and other interactive tasks.

paper_title: VISTA: A Visual Harness for Reasoning in an Interactive World
paper_authors: Qiushi Han, Keya Hu, Linlu Qiu, Cathy Wu, Kaiming He
